_note: FULL-SHELL BOARD, measured live at 1440x900 — the board's own frame size.
Per the brief: what is joined here is what this board is ABOUT (its state).
The chassis the four Shell-state boards redraw identically is skipped, with
the reason, rather than re-asserted four times:
the TOPBAR (682:2657 and its children) — boards.json carries
authority=code:topbar against all twelve 'Shell state N' boards, decided
2026-08-17 on evidence: they draw Exit | name | Saved pill | review pill |
bell | Publish(disabled) and no Quick preview, Comments or Issues chip,
while the shipped topbar has all three. The boards lose because they
contradict the board SET — 200:2 is named 'Comment mode' and its own
topbar has no comments control, and the Issues chip is what opens board
1168:4732. The same snapshot also draws Publish grey/disabled on a
returning user with content, which would mean nobody could ever publish.
The topbar has its own spec (`topbar`) and its own recipe (shell-default).
the RAIL (2034:8392) — the board fills it --color/bg-app #F3F4F6; the
shipped rail is white. That is one reading against the rail as it appears
on every other family's boards, and the rail is chassis shared by all four
of these boards plus shell-default. Not re-settled from a state board.
the CANVAS TOOLBAR (463:3962 and its ~40 chips) — one floating component
redrawn on all four boards; it belongs to the canvas family, not to a
state. Board 202:2's own walk (boards.json, 2026-08-17) already fixed the
real defect it exposed, which was the bar not wrapping at 1280.
the FOOTER BAR itself (65:196 / 66:196-equivalent) — the <footer> element
REACHED LIVE, entirely through shipped controls: dismiss the first-run
coach, insert three elements from Insert, then Cmd+A
(useCanvasKeyboard.ts:80-86 -> `composer.selection.selectAll()`). No
fixture sets the selection. `measure.mjs`'s click step carries no modifier
keys, which is why select-all rather than three shift-clicks.
The coach must be dismissed FIRST and that is a finding, not a
convenience: RailCoach is a fixed bubble at 240x154 anchored beside the
rail (x 72..312, y 152..306) and the shell opens the Insert drawer on
session start, so on first run the coach sits ON TOP of the drawer's first
six rows and eats their clicks. Measured — Playwright's click on
`insert-el-Heading` times out on intercepted pointer events until 'Got it'
is pressed. See the report.

NOT JOINED, this board only:
the ALIGN and DISTRIBUTE BUTTONS (66:205-66:223) — this board draws nine

Board 159:123 (Inspector · multi-select) draws the same control as icon
buttons, and boards.json already settles this pair at

the batch style ROWS (1709:8395-8414) — Background / Text color / Radius
/ Padding / Font size with 24-tall 160-wide inputs. Those are ColorInput
and InputWithUnit, shared with the single-selection inspector and every
profile board; a state board does not re-size them. The panel's HINT is
measured (and is 11px --bk-ink-muted as 1709:8415 asks) but not joined
either: the board gives it width 272 against a 300 frame with no stroke,
and the shipped inspector's own 1px border takes the same run to 270.
the canvas count badge and floating align toolbar — 66:4 draws neither,
but it also draws only ONE selection ring for a three-element selection,
so its canvas art is the single-select frame reused. boards.json recorded

the AI chip on this panel (measured as `ai-chip`, no join) — 66:4's
inspector header has no AI entry at all; it comes from 159:123, the same
board that settles the buttons.
CONTRAST SWEEP IS SCOPED to the multi-select panel, not the whole shell,
and that is a deliberate narrowing with a report attached. Sweeping `body`
in this state surfaces 14 text failures and 1 icon failure that belong to
the CANVAS OVERLAY layer, not to this board: the floating align toolbar
inside `.bd-selection-box` (8 glyphs, rgb(184,181,173) on the box's
rgb(225,239,254), 1.75:1), the element badge (2 runs, --bk-ink on
rgb(10,10,10), 1.12:1), and CanvasBreadcrumb (4 runs, --bk-gray-400 on its
rgba(17,24,39,0.5) bar over white, 1.34:1), plus one 12x12 icon at 1.93:1
against the 3:1 non-text floor. boards.json already records that 66:4 draws
neither the badge nor the align toolbar, so none of them is this board
conforming to anything — they are an a11y arc of their own. They are NOT
baselined here; they are excluded by scope and named, in the recipe and in
the report.
THE ALIGN LABEL IS MEASURED BUT NOT JOINED, and that is the one place on
this surface where a board loses on purpose. 66:204 names the label
--color/ink-muted. Board 159:123 fills the ALIGN band --bk-bg-subtle (a
reading measured off that frame and asserted by MultiSelectToolbar's own
test, 'tints the ALIGN section'), and 11px ink-muted on that fill is 4.39:1
against WCAG's 4.5 floor — measured in this run. Taking the board's token
would ship a contrast failure; --bk-ink-soft on the same band is 6.78:1 and
is what now ships. Said loudly here rather than baselined: the two boards
are individually right and jointly illegible, and the band is the half a
family board settled.
